questions.q: What makes Asia's AI ecosystem different from Silicon Valley's?
questions.a: Asia's AI growth runs on two engines at once: top-down government programs and bottom-up startups. Many Asian governments actively partner with startups by sharing data, offering sandboxes and even co-developing products. Builders in the region also tend to focus on practical tools shaped by local languages, infrastructure and culture.

questions.q: How is China approaching artificial intelligence?
questions.a: China is taking a top-down approach, with the stated goal of leading the world in AI by 2030. That plan includes large government funding, smart city pilots like Xiong'an New Area and a strong pipeline of AI PhDs. Provinces and cities such as Zhejiang and Shenzhen compete to become AI hubs by offering subsidies, sandboxes and supercomputing access.

questions.q: What kinds of AI startups are growing in India and Southeast Asia?
questions.a: Startups in India and Southeast Asia focus on hyper-local problems where public infrastructure has gaps. Examples from the post include KissanAI's crop advice for farmers by SMS, the Wysa mental health chatbot, inventory systems for small shops in Indonesia and AI tutors for rural students in Vietnam. These solutions are increasingly attracting global investors.

questions.q: Why is Singapore important for AI in Asia?
questions.a: Singapore acts as the region's AI policy lab and a bridge between compliance and creativity. Its AI Verify framework sets clear governance standards, and programs like SGInnovate support applied AI startups. Many multinational AI companies have chosen Singapore for their regional headquarters.

questions.q: What should businesses know before using AI in Asian markets?
questions.a: There's no single AI capital in Asia, so you'll be working with several centers that each have their own strengths. A product that works in one country can flop in the next, which makes localization core to product-market fit. Governments in many markets also act as partners, so it pays to understand local policy early.
